summary: Dwaarit grocery app first-pass: 26/26 backend pytest cases PASS (auth, products, admin product CRUD, orders, admin order status). Frontend customer flow (login routing, products list + categories + search, add-to-cart, cart with qty stepper + total, checkout form, COD order via backend) all render and function. Admin flow (login routes to /(admin)/orders, sees all customer orders, products list with edit/delete actions, modal form) renders correctly. Two real frontend bugs found: (1) literal '\n' rendered in admin orders address card, (2) URL/group collision + missing role guards on (tabs) and (admin) layouts cause customer hitting /orders directly (e.g., from order-success 'Track order') to resolve to admin layout and trigger 403. Backend is solid; frontend needs route guards + one JSX fix.

minor.issue: InsecureKeyLengthWarning: HMAC key 28 bytes (<32). Use a 32+ byte JWT_SECRET in backend/.env.

ui_bugs.issue:
Address line shows literal '
' because the escape is outside a JS expression in JSX. File: /app/frontend/app/(admin)/orders.tsx:136. Verified in screenshot: 'TEST Buyer · 5551234567
1 Test St, Testville 12345'. Fix: move the address composition into an expression — e.g. <Text>{`${a.full_name} · ${a.phone}
${a.line1}${a.line2 ? ', '+a.line2 : ''}, ${a.city} ${a.pincode}`}</Text>.

integration_issues.issue: Both app/(tabs)/orders.tsx and app/(admin)/orders.tsx serve the URL /orders. On the web preview, a customer that navigates to /orders directly (which is what happens after order-success 'Track order' invokes router.replace('/(tabs)/orders'), and what the browser address bar shows) lands on the ADMIN orders layout. The screen then calls GET /api/admin/orders and the backend correctly returns 403 ('admin orders load failed: Admin only'). Same risk for /products. Neither (tabs)/_layout.tsx nor (admin)/_layout.tsx has a role guard. Fix: add a role guard at each layout — in (admin)/_layout.tsx redirect non-admins to /(tabs)/home; in (tabs)/_layout.tsx redirect admins to /(admin)/orders. Also consider renaming admin routes (e.g., /admin/orders, /admin/products) to avoid URL collision.

Zustand cart store is global and is NOT cleared on sign-out (only on successful checkout via clear()). If a customer signs out with items in cart and a different user signs in, the previous cart leaks. Recommend calling useCart.getState().clear() inside AuthContext.signOut(). (Not blocking but a real correctness issue.)

issues: Console warns: 'shadow*' style props are deprecated, use boxShadow (RN Web). Several theme tokens (shadow.soft/card) still emit shadowColor/shadowOffset/shadowRadius. Non-blocking on native, noisy on web.
Console warns: props.pointerEvents is deprecated; use style.pointerEvents. Coming from a child component (likely PrimaryButton/TextField). Non-blocking.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/app/(admin)/orders.tsx:136 — wrap the address text inside a JS template literal so \n becomes a real newline.

Add role guards to /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx and /app/frontend/app/(admin)/_layout.tsx using useAuth(): redirect to /(auth)/login if no user, and cross-redirect when role mismatches the layout group.
Optionally rename admin routes from (admin) group to /admin/* (move files to app/admin/orders.tsx etc.) to eliminate the /orders & /products URL collision between (tabs) and (admin) groups.
Clear cart on sign-out in AuthContext.signOut() to avoid leaking cart between users.
Set JWT_SECRET in backend/.env to a 32+ byte value to silence InsecureKeyLengthWarning.
critical_code_review_comments: (admin)/orders.tsx:136 — '\n' written as JSX text (not inside a {`...`} expression) renders literally. Confirmed visually.

(tabs)/_layout.tsx and (admin)/_layout.tsx have NO role/auth guard — any authenticated (or even unauth, since web Expo Router doesn't auto-redirect) user can deep-link into either group. Auth-check belongs in the group layouts via <Redirect/>.
cartStore is a singleton zustand store with no per-user namespacing and signOut() does not clear it.
URL collision: two routes resolve to /orders and /products. Expo Router does not guarantee which wins for direct URL nav — observed admin layout taking precedence on web.
server.py JWT secret length below 32 bytes triggers PyJWT InsecureKeyLengthWarning.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% — login/home/cart/checkout-form/admin-orders/admin-products render and APIs wire up; routing/role-guard bug + admin address \n bug remain

seed_data_creation: No persistent seed created. pytest creates unique TEST_ users via signup, one TEST product (created → patched → deleted, leaves DB clean), and one COD order from the demo customer that is left in 'delivered' state (visible in /api/admin/orders). Safe to leave or wipe.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_dwaarit_api.py is the regression baseline — re-run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. Credentials live in /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Frontend mobile viewport 390x844. Note: web preview at http://localhost:3000 mirrors public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL via /api routing. After fixes, verify: (a) customer 'Track order' lands on customer Orders tab (NOT admin), (b) admin orders screen shows address on two lines, (c) signing out clears the cart. The 'shadow*' and 'pointerEvents' console warnings are React Native Web noise, not blockers.
rca_of_issue: Admin/customer route collision RCA: Expo Router groups `(tabs)` and `(admin)` both define `orders.tsx` and (admin also) `products.tsx`. Group parentheses are not part of the URL, so both produce the SAME URL (/orders, /products). When the user navigates via a typed URL or a deep-link `router.replace('/(tabs)/orders')` on web, the router strips the group and resolves to whichever route registered first; testing shows the (admin) variant winning on /orders. Combined with the absence of role guards in either layout, customers can render the admin screen, which immediately fails its GET /api/admin/orders with 403. Mitigation: (i) add role guards via <Redirect/> in both layouts using useAuth(); (ii) rename admin routes to a distinct URL prefix (e.g., move app/(admin)/* → app/admin/*), eliminating the collision at the URL level.
